record.vts_name: Vessel Traffic Service Prince William Sound
record.vts_centre: Valdez Traffic (Vessel Traffic Center Valdez / Prince William Sound)
record.vts_sector: Valdez Arm VTS Special Area applies to the Valdez Arm TSS (§161.60(b))
record.vts_boundary_basis: VTS area: US navigable waters north of the Cape Hinchinbrook Light to Schooner Rock Light line, between 146°30'W and 147°20'W (§161.60(a), V-S1). The PWS TSS lanes run from 60°20.6'N to 60°49.5'N, 146°48'W to 147°04'W and the Valdez Arm TSS to 60°58.9'N (§§167.1702-1703, V-S2); all points are north of the reporting points at Schooner Rock (60°18'42"N) and Cape Hinchinbrook and within the longitude limits. The Valdez Arm VTS Special Area is defined by the Valdez Arm TSS. The Cape Hinchinbrook precautionary area (§167.1701(a)) extends to 59°51.80'N and 146°00.01'W, south of the VTS line and partly south of the VMRS limit of 60°00'N.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers Prince William Sound. VMRS reporting to Valdez Traffic (Table 161.12(c)(9)) and reporting points under §161.60 are VTS duties, not a separate MRS.
record.unresolved_issue: Coverage is full for the traffic lanes and separation zones; the southern part of the associated Cape Hinchinbrook precautionary area is outside the VTS area (and partly outside the VMRS area). Light position for Cape Hinchinbrook Light taken from the reporting-point coordinates, not the Light List.
record.evidence_summary: 33 CFR 161.60 (eCFR 1 Sept 2026) defines the VTS PWS area and names the Valdez Arm TSS as a VTS Special Area; the TSS lanes and separation zones (33 CFR 167.1702-1703) lie inside the VTS area. USCG NAVCEN lists Prince William Sound among operating VTCs.
record.source_date: 2026-09-01 (eCFR point in time); §161.60 last amended 3 Apr 2024
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only with VTS Prince William Sound; boundary re-checked against eCFR 2026-09-01

record.vts_name: Cooperative Vessel Traffic Service (CVTS) for the Juan de Fuca Region
record.vts_authority: Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS) and US Coast Guard, jointly under the 1979 CVTS agreement
record.vts_centre: Prince Rupert Traffic (CCG MCTS Prince Rupert), VHF 74
record.vts_sector: Prince Rupert Traffic sector of the CVTS (waters west of 124°40'W)
record.vts_boundary_basis: RAMN 2026 s.3.5.4 (V-S5) defines the CVTS Area of Operation as 124°40'W south along the Washington coast to 48°00'N, west to 125°15'W and north to 48°35'45"N, and requires inbound vessels to check in with Prince Rupert Traffic 'prior to entering the traffic separation scheme'. US Table 161.12(c)(10)(iii) (V-S1) likewise gives Prince Rupert Traffic the waters north of 48°00'N and east of 125°15'W, west of 124°40'W. The western approach (48°27.3'N-48°32.1'N, 125°04.67'W-125°09.00'W, §167.1301, V-S2) lies wholly inside this area. Statutory zones are narrower: US VTS Puget Sound area stops at the US territorial sea (§161.55) and the Canadian Prince Rupert VTS Zone at the Canadian territorial sea (V-S4); by my approximate plot most of this TSS is beyond 12 nm from both coasts.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the Juan de Fuca region. Canadian VTS Zone reporting (SOR/2025-275) and US VMRS reporting (33 CFR 161) are VTS duties recorded under the services, not a separate MRS.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: CVTS participation outside Canadian and US territorial waters is not mandatory (V-S5), so reporting there is in effect voluntary
record.unresolved_issue: 33 CFR 161.55(a) defines the CVTS for the Juan de Fuca Region with a western limit near 124°48'W, narrower than the RAMN CVTS Area of Operation (125°15'W); coverage relies on RAMN s.3.5.4 and Table 161.12(c). RAMN quotes were extracted through WebFetch because direct download failed. Territorial-sea distances are my approximations.
record.evidence_summary: Official CCG publication defines the CVTS area to 125°15'W and 48°00'N and ties the Prince Rupert Traffic check-in to entry into the TSS; the US regulation's table assigns the same box to Prince Rupert Traffic. The TSS lies inside that service area; mandatory participation applies only within territorial waters.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS association confirmed but re-based on RAMN 2026 CVTS area and Table 161.12(c); prior claim that the Canadian VTS Zone/12 nm area contains the TSS not supported (statutory zones end at the territorial sea); Victoria Traffic not relevant to this component

record.vts_authority: Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS) and US Coast Guard, jointly under the 1979 CVTS agreement
record.vts_centre: Prince Rupert Traffic (CCG MCTS Prince Rupert), VHF 74
record.vts_sector: Prince Rupert Traffic sector of the CVTS (waters west of 124°40'W)
record.vts_boundary_basis: South-western approach (48°22.55'N-48°27.63'N, 125°00.81'W-125°09.00'W, §167.1302, V-S2) lies wholly inside the CVTS Area of Operation (to 125°15'W and 48°00'N) in RAMN 2026 s.3.5.4 (V-S5) and inside the Table 161.12(c)(10)(iii) Prince Rupert Traffic area (V-S1). It lies south of the international boundary; by my approximate plot only its north-eastern end is within about 12 nm of Tatoosh Island, so most of it is outside the US VTS Puget Sound statutory area (§161.55).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the Juan de Fuca region. Canadian VTS Zone reporting (SOR/2025-275) and US VMRS reporting (33 CFR 161) are VTS duties recorded under the services, not a separate MRS.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: CVTS participation outside Canadian and US territorial waters is not mandatory (V-S5), so reporting there is in effect voluntary
record.unresolved_issue: Same as TSS-0163 (narrower CVTS definition in §161.55(a); RAMN extracted via WebFetch; approximate territorial-sea plot).
record.evidence_summary: As for TSS-0163: CVTS service area (RAMN 2026) and US Table 161.12(c) Prince Rupert Traffic area contain the south-western approach; mandatory participation only within territorial waters.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS association confirmed on RAMN CVTS area and Table 161.12(c); Victoria Traffic removed; statutory Canadian zone does not cover this component (it is south of the boundary)

record.vts_name: Cooperative Vessel Traffic Service (CVTS) for the Juan de Fuca Region
record.vts_authority: US Coast Guard (VTS Puget Sound) and Canadian Coast Guard (MCTS), jointly under the CVTS agreement
record.vts_centre: Seattle Traffic (USCG VTS Puget Sound) east of 124°40'W; Prince Rupert Traffic (CCG MCTS) west of 124°40'W
record.vts_sector: Seattle Traffic VHF 5A sector (east of 124°40'W); Prince Rupert Traffic VHF 74 sector (west of 124°40'W)
record.vts_boundary_basis: Western lanes run from 125°00'W to 123°31.98'W along 48°13'N-48°32'N (§167.1311, V-S2). East of 124°40'W: US waters are in the VTS Puget Sound area and the Seattle Traffic Ch 5A area (§161.55, Table 161.12(c)(10)(ii), V-S1); Canadian waters are in the statutory Victoria VTS Zone, whose boundary follows the international boundary through Juan de Fuca Strait to 48°28'36"N 124°40'W (V-S4), and are managed by Seattle Traffic under the CVTS (RAMN s.3.5.4, V-S5). West of 124°40'W: Canadian waters are in the Prince Rupert VTS Zone (V-S4) and US waters within the US territorial sea are in the VTS Puget Sound area; the whole segment is inside the CVTS Area of Operation and the Prince Rupert Traffic Table 161.12(c) area. The §161.55(a) CVTS area (west limit about 124°48'W) also covers most of the lanes.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the Juan de Fuca region. Canadian VTS Zone reporting (SOR/2025-275) and US VMRS reporting (33 CFR 161) are VTS duties recorded under the services, not a separate MRS.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: CVTS participation outside Canadian and US territorial waters is not mandatory (V-S5), so reporting there is in effect voluntary
record.unresolved_issue: Coordinator to decide whether the CVTS is recorded as one VTS entity or as links to its component services (VTS Puget Sound, Prince Rupert and Victoria VTS Zones). SOR/2025-275 in-force date not verified.
record.evidence_summary: Statutory US (33 CFR 161.55) and Canadian (SOR/2025-275) VTS areas and the joint CVTS together cover the whole of the western lanes; centres Seattle Traffic and Prince Rupert Traffic split at 124°40'W.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS association confirmed; operating centres are Seattle Traffic and Prince Rupert Traffic (Victoria VTS Zone covers Canadian waters east of 124°40'W but is managed by Seattle Traffic under the CVTS); finding checked for this individual component
